newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan recovery likely to be maintained - BOJ outlook.
newsitem.headline: Japan recovery likely to be maintained - BOJ outlook.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery likely to be maintained on the whole in the coming months, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in its quarterly economic outlook on Friday.
"A slow but steady favourable cycle is at work, whereby growth in domestic private-sector demand leads to increases in production and income.
"Also, downward pressure on the economy stemming from (a decline in) net exports is expected to ease. Thus, the recovery trend on the whole is likely to be maintained in the future," the report said.
However, the report added that pressure from various structural adjustments remained in addition to fiscal policies which would restrain the economy.
The report said prices are unlikely to go into a decisive upward trend because of a slow recovery in supply-and-demand conditions and intense global competition.

The drop in Japanese prices is starting to decelerate due to a rise in import prices stemming from the yen's weakness and higher crude oil prices, as well as improvements in the domestic supply-and-demand situation.

The decline in Japan's net exports is expected to taper off gradually due to the effect of the weaker yen, although structural factors such as the shift of production bases abroad would keep exports in check, the BOJ said.

Public-sector investment for public works projects is likely to decrease, but investment in housing will likely stay at current high levels, supported by low interest rates and a recent decrease in condominium inventories, it said.

The report said long-term interest rates and rates on three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) "have both declined significantly" since mid-July because market expectations of higher interest rates had receded.

Japan's money supply is continuing year-on-year growth of between three and four percent as lending by private financial firms is slow due to weak corporate demand for capital and the fact that companies are looking to financial markets for funds, the BOJ said.

Corporate capital spending will likely continue recovering on the back of a rebound in companies' profits, progress in stock adjustments and strong growth in the telecommunications industry, the report said.
Consumer spending will also continue to recover due to increases in income, it said.
The report said the decline in the trade surplus in real terms took a breather and the nominal current account surplus expanded in the July-September quarter of this year, it said.
However, it added that the July-September quarter data was not enough to ascertain that the decline in Japan's external balance had bottomed out.
